subject: POC stability: shortfall coverage vs. credit extension
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sam Li <sam@orchidai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC stability: shortfall coverage vs. credit extension

Hi Sam —

Hope the team's tests are going well. I pulled the usage report for the last 10 days and we can see OrchidAI's burst demand spiked above the expected token cap on two occasions (attached: orchid-poc-usage-report.csv). I wanted to surface two pragmatic remediation paths so you can pick what fits engineering and procurement timelines: 

1) Timeboxed extension (3 business days): we keep your current ratecard and extend the POC window by 72 hours so your integration team can finish the full run.
2) Credit buffer (one-off token credit): Redwood applies a one-time credit to cover the shortfall (equivalent to ~48 hours of sustained burst) while keeping the original POC end date.

Tradeoffs: extension buys more runway for functional validation but delays procurement timelines; credit avoids date changes but reduces the demonstrable runtime you can measure.

If you want, I can draft a compact amendment for procurement (we can route it through DocuSign). Laura and Grace — looping you in for pricing approval and CS impact.

Next steps: Sam, tell us which option you prefer and if procurement needs an exact $ figure or just a credit token amount.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: orchid-poc-usage-report.csv (csv)
From: Sam Li <sam@orchidai.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC stability: shortfall coverage vs. credit extension

Thanks, Dev — appreciate the quick analysis. Grace, this matches what our infra team saw overnight. We're weight-testing the model on longer sequences which caused the burst. Procurement prefers not to move the POC end date (tight budget window this quarter).

Could you quantify the credit option in token-equivalent + a dollar estimate? If the credit is clean (single-line invoice credit) we can accept and still run the same experiments before the original cut-off.

Also, small ask: can you add a temporary higher concurrency cap for the next 48 hours to smooth retries while we ramp down? If that's operationally feasible, it'll reduce the token burn from failures.

Sam
CTO, OrchidAI

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sam Li <sam@orchidai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC stability: shortfall coverage vs. credit extension

Sam — great, thanks for the preference. Quick answers: 

- Credit sizing: based on the attached usage, the shortfall is ~1.9M tokens. We can offer a straight credit of 2.0M tokens which we estimate at $3,600 at your current POC rate.
- Concurrency bump: operationally feasible as a temporary policy for 48 hours. We'll set a soft cap increase and monitor for backpressure. Grace, can your CS ops team confirm we can schedule the bump for Tue 08/25 09:00 PT and auto-revert 48 hours later?

If Sam approves, I'll prepare a one-line credit memo + amendment PDF and send to procurement. Laura, for referrals: does 2.0M tokens / $3,600 need additional commercial approval or is that inside our regional concession threshold?

Cheers,
Dev

Attachments: optional-amendment-draft.pdf (pdf)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sam Li <sam@orchidai.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC stability: shortfall coverage vs. credit extension

Dev — approved. 2.0M token credit / $3,600 sits within regional seat-based concession limits for POCs under $10k. No further legal redlines required for a single-line credit memo. Grace, please proceed with the concurrency bump scheduling.

Two operational notes for CS: 
- Add a short summary to the POC Success Plan capturing the burst cause and the mitigation (concurrency + credit).
- Capture a clear acceptance metric before the POC close (e.g., successful 24-hour sustained run at target qps with <2% error rate).

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Li <sam@orchidai.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC stability: shortfall coverage vs. credit extension

Sam / team — scheduling confirmed. We'll increase the concurrency cap at Tue 08/25 09:00 PT and auto-revert 48 hours later (Wed 08/27 09:00 PT). I updated the POC Success Plan in the shared Drive link (https://redwood.app/drive/orchid-poc-notes) with the acceptance metric Laura noted.

Sam: one more operational ask — please confirm the precise S3 path where logs will land after the runs (so our reliability engineering team can pull error traces if needed). Also confirm you approve the 2.0M token credit / $3,600 and I will attach the credit memo to the HubSpot deal record and route the amendment for signature if procurement needs it.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
